item.title: UK to deploy fighter jets, military advisers to Saudi Arabia as defence from Houthi attacks
item.description:
UK to deploy fighter jets, military advisers to Saudi Arabia as defence from Houthi attacks

The UK is set to deploy Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets to Saudi Arabia as a form of protection against Houthi attack.

According to the British government announcement, the aircraft will only be used to conduct defensive missions against Houthi missile and drone strikes, but will not be utilised to attack Houthis. 

Military advisers as well as an  RAF A400M transport aircraft will also be sent to the kingdom to provide support. 

"The continuing attacks from the Houthis on our ally Saudi Arabia are absolutely despicable," Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting said.

"The targeting of the airport in Riyadh in particular shows the lengths the Houthis are going to escalate the situation in the region," he added.

item.title: Trump says Iran has a 'dream' for war to continue after US midterm elections
item.description:
Trump says Iran has a 'dream' for war to continue after US midterm elections

US President Donald Trump claimed that Iran has a "dream" for the war to remain ongoing beyond the November midterm elections.

"Well, it’ll end very fast. As soon as the war ends – and it will end one way or the other very quickly – oil is going to drop like a rock," Trump said during a campaign rally in North Carolina

He added that the rise of energy prices were a "very small price to pay for keeping a nuclear weapon away from the world’s number one state sponsor of terror".

item.title: Saudi attacks on boats in Yemen's Taiz kills eight fishermen
item.description:
Saudi attacks on boats in Yemen's Taiz kills eight fishermen

The Ministry of Health and Environment announced that Saudi strikes targeting boats off the coast of al-Kadha in the Taiz Governorate killed eight fishermen.

The ministry of Health slammed the attack as a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law, saying that the kingdom continues to target civilians and  civilian objects.

item.description:
Critics said images of detained former leader were a stunt by the military to end country’s diplomatic isolation

Myanmar has delivered presents from Britain’s ​King Charles to Aung San Suu Kyi, releasing rare photos of the imprisoned former leader in what critics said was a stunt by the country’s military to end diplomatic isolation.

A presidential spokesperson said on social media that home ministry officials handed over two gardening books on soil, “along with one sealed envelope and a sealed diplomatic pouch”, from King Charles, who is known to have an interest in planting and the environment.

item.title: Houthi attack kills 53 in biggest single loss of life since Yemen civil war reignited
item.description:
More than 200 mostly young people said to be injured after ballistic missile attack on training camp for government forces

At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government security forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September.

The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to have injured more than 200 others, mostly young recruits, and was described as a disaster by the country’s UN-recognised government. The injured were taken from the police and army training camp in the Jardan district to a hospital in the local capital, Ataq, where pleas for blood donations were made.
